title: Wait for a response
intro: A caller asks a remote service for CI status. Network travel and processing both take time; the caller waits for the response.
takeaway: A successful response supplies evidence about the request. Every time in this sequence is an illustrative policy value.

beats.text: The caller asks for CI status. The remote service must answer.
The service processes the request. The caller is waiting.
A response arrives in time. The caller can use the reported status.
Some responses take too long. A timeout bounds one attempt.

title: A timeout is not a rollback
intro: The caller stops waiting when its attempt timeout expires. Work at the remote service may continue.
takeaway: Missing a response means the outcome is unknown. Cancellation and rollback require their own implementation.

beats.text: The caller is still waiting. The remote request is in progress.
The attempt timeout expires. The caller stops waiting now.
Remote work may still continue. A timeout does not undo that work.
Report the outcome as unknown. Do not invent a failed build result.

title: Retry only when safe
intro: A retry is another attempt at the same operation. A status read can usually be retried, but effectful operations need a safe retry contract.
takeaway: Decide retry safety from the operation contract. An idempotency key can help protect a write when the service implements it.

beats.text: The first status read timed out. Another attempt may obtain the result.
Check whether repetition is safe. This operation only reads CI status.
Send a second bounded attempt. It is the same question, asked again.
Use the response if it arrives. A write would need its own contract.

title: Back off before retrying
intro: After a shared failure, callers can retry together and add another burst of load. Backoff waits; jitter varies the wait between callers. These delays are illustrative.
takeaway: Different retry delays spread arrivals. They do not guarantee recovery, and total attempts still need a bound.

beats.text: Three callers encounter the same failure. Immediate retries would form a new burst.
Each caller chooses a retry delay. Jitter makes those delays different.
Watch the retries arrive at different times. The service still may not recover.
Each caller has made two attempts. Keep further retries within a limit.

title: Bound the whole operation
intro: An attempt timeout and an overall deadline solve different problems. In this illustrative policy, two attempts and their delay must fit within twelve seconds. Animation time is slowed for explanation.
takeaway: Five seconds for the first attempt plus a two-second delay leaves at most five seconds for a retry, less overhead. The deadline gate rejects further attempts when the shared budget reaches zero.

beats.text: Example policy: a 12-second deadline. The gate permits the first attempt.
Attempt 1 times out after 5 seconds. The shared budget has 7 seconds left.
A 2-second backoff leaves at most 5s. The second attempt uses that remainder.
The deadline expires: no third attempt. Return unknown and both timed-out tries.
